content: This document provides a summary of information about the medication Cefotetan. It is important to note that this summary does not include all possible details about the product and does not guarantee that the medication is safe, effective, or appropriate for your specific condition. This information is not a substitute for personalized medical advice. Always consult your healthcare provider for complete information about this medication and your individual health needs. Cefotetan, commonly sold under the brand name Cefotan, is an antibiotic used to treat a wide range of bacterial infections. It is also administered before and during certain surgical procedures to help prevent infections. This medication belongs to the cephalosporin class of antibiotics and is effective only against bacterial infections. It is not effective for viral infections, such as the common cold or flu. Instructions for Use: Carefully read and follow all preparation and usage instructions provided by the manufacturer. Consult your pharmacist for additional guidance. Before use, visually inspect the product for particles or discoloration. If using a frozen pre-mixed solution, thaw the container at room temperature or in the refrigerator. If thawed in the refrigerator, allow the solution to sit at room temperature for at least one hour before use. Do not thaw the solution using a water bath or microwave. After thawing, shake the container well and check for leaks by squeezing it. Discard the solution if the container leaks. For optimal effectiveness, administer this antibiotic at evenly spaced intervals. To help you remember, use the medication at the same time(s) each day. Continue using the medication for the full prescribed treatment period, even if symptoms improve after a few days. Learn how to safely store and dispose of needles and medical supplies. Possible Side Effects: Common side effects may include swelling, redness, pain, or soreness at the injection site. Rarely, this medication may cause loss of appetite, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, or headache. Remember that your doctor has prescribed this medication because they believe the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. In rare cases, Cefotetan may cause a severe intestinal condition known as Clostridium difficile-associated diarrhea, which can occur during treatment or weeks to months after treatment has stopped. Prolonged or repeated use of this medication may lead to oral thrush or a new vaginal yeast infection. Serious allergic reactions to this drug are rare but possible. This is not a complete list of potential side effects. If you experience any unusual symptoms, contact your doctor. Precautions: Before using Cefotetan, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, other cephalosporins, penicillins, or any other substances. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. Avoid consuming alcoholic beverages while taking this medication and for at least three days after completing it, as this may cause adverse reactions. Cefotetan may reduce the effectiveness of live bacterial vaccines, such as the typhoid vaccine. This medication can pass into breast milk, so consult your doctor if you are breastfeeding. Drug Interactions: Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal supplements, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Cefotetan may interfere with certain laboratory tests, such as urine glucose tests or serum/urine creatinine tests, potentially causing false results. Overdose: If someone has overdosed and exhibits serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call emergency services immediately (911 in the U.S.). Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. Storage: Different brands or packaging of this medication may have specific storage requirements. Check the product packaging for instructions or consult your pharmacist. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information was last revised in September 2024. Always consult your healthcare provider for the most accurate and personalized guidance regarding this medication.
